text.display: On the sixteenth of July, 1969, a Saturn Five rocket lifted three men off the Earth. Seen from the command module Columbia, the lunar module Eagle carried Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin down to the Moon. Then came the words: Houston, Tranquility Base here. The Eagle has landed. Armstrong took this photograph of Aldrin. Look into the visor, and you can see Armstrong himself. Aldrin photographed his own bootprint, to study the lunar soil. On the twenty-fourth of July, all three splashed down home.
